amber-pulse.$description: Amber Pulse — Yellow supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

cream-paper.$description: Cream Paper — Page background and outer canvas. Borrowed from Notion's own workspace palette to position Super as its native publishing layer

white-card.$description: White Card — Card and elevated surface that sits on Cream Paper. Provides subtle separation through brightness contrast rather than shadow

ink-charcoal.$description: Ink Charcoal — Primary text, dominant foreground color, nav elements, and high-emphasis UI. The workhorse neutral of the entire system

notion-charcoal.$description: Notion Charcoal — Secondary text and borders within card contexts. Slightly warmer than Ink Charcoal, echoes Notion's native text color

steel-body.$description: Steel Body — Supporting neutral for secondary UI, dividers, and muted labels.

slate-mute.$description: Slate Mute — Near-gray with a faint cool tint, used for very low-emphasis body content and subtle borders

carbon.$description: Carbon — Heading emphasis, high-contrast dark surface for footer and dark feature sections, near-black for strong typographic moments

black.$description: Black — Footer background and deepest dark surface. The maximum darkness level in the surface stack

hairline.$description: Hairline — Hairline borders, dividers, and subtle structural lines. The lightest visible neutral that still reads as a defined edge

silver-divider.$description: Silver Divider — Secondary borders and dividers where more visual weight is needed than Hairline

warm-taupe.$description: Warm Taupe — Subtle warm-toned text for tertiary content, gives body copy a slight paper-on-desk warmth without being obviously chromatic

beausite.$description: Custom display and body typeface used across every UI context — nav, headings, body, buttons, cards, badges. Beausite is a contemporary neo-grotesque with humanist proportions; its tight tracking at large sizes gives the hero editorial confidence, while its open counters at body sizes maintain readability. A close substitute would be Inter, Söhne, or General Sans.
